classes.name: Presidential election
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 80(1)-(4): direct election concurrently with the general election; the First Vice-President is elected on the same ticket
classes.finest_note: District in the 1994 to 2009 books, polling station for 2019, 2020, and 2025
classes.note: First held on 17 May 1994; before that the President was not chosen by popular vote (Life President from 1971). Plurality until 2019. The Constitutional Court annulled the 2019 result on 3 February 2020 and read 'majority' as more than half the valid votes; Act 13 of 2020 and Act 4 of 2023 wrote the rule into s. 80(2) with a second poll within sixty days. The fresh election of 23 June 2020 re-ran 2019. No second poll has been needed: the 2025 winner took 56.8%.

cadence.runoff_rule: s. 80(2): more than fifty percent of the valid votes, else a second poll between the top two within sixty days of the declaration

classes.name: National referendum
classes.locator: Report on the 1994 elections: the change from a one-party to a multiparty system followed the National Referendum on June 14, 1993
classes.disposition_reason: The only referendum, on 14 June 1993, was run by the National Referendum Commission, and its results by district are not on MEC's site or any other official host reachable from here. The Constitution (s. 196) requires a referendum to amend certain sections, but none has been held since.
classes.note: Multiparty system against the one-party state, 14 June 1993; the multiparty option won.

cadence.locator: Constitution, s. 76 (the Commission conducts referendums) and s. 196

classes.name: Parliamentary elections, 1964 to 1992
classes.name_en: National Assembly before the multiparty Constitution
classes.locator: Report on the 1994 elections: constituencies increased from 141 (the one-party Parliament) to 177
classes.disposition_reason: Returns were published as notices in the Malawi Gazette, which is not online, and the Parliament of Malawi's site refused automated requests (403). Many seats were returned unopposed; from 1978 voters chose among Malawi Congress Party candidates.
classes.note: Self-government general election of April 1964, then Malawi Congress Party elections under the one-party state; 141 constituencies by 1992. Years below are not yet confirmed from an official record.

classes.name: Local council elections before 1994
classes.name_en: District and town councils before the multiparty era
classes.locator: Report on the 2000 Local Government Elections: the last Local Government Elections were held in 1992
classes.disposition_reason: No official result record of the pre-1994 council elections is online; MEC's 2000 report only says the last were held in 1992.

classes.name: Nyasaland Legislative Council elections
classes.name_en: Legislative Council of Nyasaland, elected members
classes.locator: Parliament of Malawi, history of the Legislative Council
classes.disposition_reason: Colonial returns sit in the Nyasaland Government Gazette, which is not online, and the Parliament of Malawi's site refused automated requests (403).
classes.note: European members elected from 1956 on a restricted roll; the 15 August 1961 election had lower-roll and higher-roll constituencies and gave Africans a majority.

classes.name: Federal Assembly of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, Nyasaland seats
classes.name_en: Federal Assembly of Rhodesia and Nyasaland (Nyasaland constituencies)
classes.locator: Parliament of Malawi, history of representation before independence
classes.disposition_reason: The Federation's legislature (1953-1963) elected Nyasaland's members on federal rolls in 1953, 1958, and 1962; its returns are in the Federal Gazette, which is not online.

classes.name: Senate
classes.locator: Parliament of Malawi, history: the Senate provided by the 1994 Constitution
classes.disposition_reason: The 1994 Constitution provided a Senate of indirectly chosen members, but it was never constituted and was removed in 2001; no election was ever held.

classes.name: Election of the Speaker
classes.locator: Constitution, Chapter VI: the National Assembly elects its Speaker from among its members
classes.disposition_reason: An internal vote of the National Assembly at its first sitting, recorded in Hansard rather than run or published as an election.

classes.name: Election of council chairpersons and mayors
classes.locator: Local Government Act (Cap. 22:01): each council elects its chairperson or mayor from among the ward councillors
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the councillors from among themselves; there is no public ballot and MEC publishes no count.

classes.name: Traditional leaders (chiefs)
classes.locator: Chiefs Act (Cap. 22:03): the President recognizes chiefs according to customary succession
classes.disposition_reason: Chiefs succeed under customary law and are recognized by the President; there is no ballot.

classes.name: Judicial appointments
classes.name_en: Judges of the Supreme Court of Appeal and the High Court
classes.locator: Constitution, Chapter IX: the President appoints the Chief Justice, confirmed by the National Assembly, and the other judges on the recommendation of the Judicial Service Commission

classes.name: Party primary elections
classes.name_en: Party primaries for parliamentary, ward, and presidential candidates
classes.locator: Political Parties Act, 2018: parties choose their candidates under their own constitutions
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the parties under their own rules, not by MEC; results are not published officially.

classes.name: Recall of a Member of Parliament
classes.name_en: Recall of Members of the National Assembly
classes.disposition_reason: The recall provision of the 1994 Constitution was repealed in 1995 before it was ever used; no recall vote has been held.
